summary: English and Russian first-party discovery identified Nizhnevartovsk's municipal 3D geoportal and EGRN-derived land-plot layers. Viewer inspection exposed a historical WFS configuration, but bounded anonymous requests returned HTTP 404 and the municipal open-data API required an API key. No parcel polygon was retained.
queryAndRequestOutcomes: All executed queries, URLs, request statuses, viewer configuration findings, schema notes, and scope limits are recorded in city-7450-nizhnevartovsk.json.

scopeLimits: Exact WUP point [60.9389173002296, 76.567955531142] was preserved in latitude/longitude order and not shifted.
The tested WFS capabilities and bounded GetFeature requests returned HTTP 404; this is a route/access failure, not evidence of citywide absence.
The municipal open-data API returned HTTP 403 because an API_KEY was required; no key was used or sought.
Large configured KML layers were not downloaded; no raw source attributes or unsafe fields were retained.
A bounded response, if later obtained, would not establish citywide completeness. Packet completion is not source integration/admission.
uncertainty: Native parcel identity and CRS unverified
Current viewer may have changed after the captured configuration
doNotInfer: A map extent or 404 does not establish parcel absence
Municipal EGRN display does not prove a reusable open API
National EGRN custody does not imply citywide open geometry access
